title: I Guess I Haven't Learned That Yet: Discovering New Ways of Living When the Old Ways Stop Working
author: Shauna Niequist
target_audience: Adults navigating change or transition in life
Readers interested in personal growth and resilience
Followers of Shauna Niequist’s previous books
core_themes: Letting go of old habits and expectations
Curiosity and learning at any age or stage
primary_purpose: To encourage readers to face life's unexpected changes by cultivating curiosity, self-compassion, and openness to new ways of living, all while sharing the author’s personal journey of adaptation and spiritual growth.

structure_format.organization: Divided into short essays or chapters, each centered around a lesson or theme the author is learning
features: Honest reflections on faith and doubt
Practical wisdom for coping with change
Invitations for readers to reflect on their own journeys

key_concepts_lessons: Growth often requires letting go of the old ways that once worked.
Curiosity is a vital tool for facing the unknown.
Self-compassion helps process vulnerability and uncertainty.
It's okay not to have the answers; learning is a lifelong process.
Faith can be flexible and evolving, especially in seasons of crisis.
Asking new questions can lead to unexpected healing and transformation.
notable_features: Essay-style chapters for easy, reflective reading
Blends spiritual musings with practical life lessons
Relevant for those experiencing transition, loss, or new beginnings
cultural_historical_context: Published in the aftermath of the COVID-19 pandemic, the book resonates with widespread themes of loss, disruption, and personal reinvention. Shauna’s move from the Midwest to New York City and her evolving spiritual journey mirror the upheaval many faced globally.
reception_impact: Well-received by fans for its authenticity and relatability
Popular in Christian and general self-help book circles
Praised for its gentle encouragement and real-life honesty
Serves as a comfort to readers dealing with uncertainty or transition
comparable_titles: Present Over Perfect by Shauna Niequist
Everything Happens for a Reason: And Other Lies I’ve Loved by Kate Bowler
